clue.text: Nick regularly bribed horse moving near Scottish actor

parts.note: to nick is to steal, as is to rob

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse

indicators.note: moving tells us the letters of the next word shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief, a bribe and a horse wandering towards a Scottish film star: a crime caper in the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks B, I, E from 'bribed'; 'moving' rearranges NEAR into RANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbie Coltrane was a Glasgow-born actor, famous as Hagrid in the Harry Potter films.

clue.text: Odd British outsiders in Lodge uncover secrecy perhaps

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd

indicators.note: outsiders in takes the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Strange goings-on at a Masonic lodge lead to secrets being exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumble a plot is to discover what was hidden, so exposing secrecy is an example.

clue.text: Key exam covers last part of the term in geology

explanation.walkthrough: AS level is a British exam taken at about seventeen. 'the' in 'the term' is fodder, not grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology this is the lowest point to which a river can erode its bed, usually sea level.

clue.text: Separated from where rail passengers sit, according to Jonathan Ross?

clue.text: 'Beef' not opened, when revealed as horse

clue.text: Some pirates embarked, having turned over Spanish land

clue.text: Fruit crop in headland one hundred in total

clue.text: Vegan food, one of five consumed daily, in seconds

clue.text: Manage to take middle out of Japanese fencing with relative

clue.text: Swaggering adventurer not having wash basin, initially — pig?

taken as written

clue.text: Refuse to wipe clean his pants — black's ingrained
